answer: The pourer ladles his glue into the joints, and the ladle must measure true or the joint turns weak. Stave ash hoop fitter chime writ is the ladling: a writ ash hoop fitters sign after fitting yard checks. The terrace is the first ladle, poured at the joint; the atlas is the last, poured before the glue sets, and the bridge is the joint itself, tight as a drum. A cheat must ladle 83 false joints and set 83 false barrels.
